expectations.text: G1: Identifies that the route handler calls the repository directly instead of going through an application/use-case layer
expectations.evidence: "Controller calls the repository directly — no use case in between... There is no application/ layer here at all."

expectations.text: G2: Identifies that the void-invoice invariant (Invoice.markPaid()) is bypassed because the route updates the row directly, i.e. flags the resulting reachable bug, not just the structural smell
expectations.evidence: "the pay route never constructs or touches an Invoice domain object... A void invoice can be marked 'paid' through this endpoint with no invariant check whatsoever" — called out as 'the critical bug.'

expectations.text: G3: Identifies that the raw DB row is returned directly from the GET endpoint instead of a mapped DTO/domain-shaped response
expectations.evidence: "Raw DB row returned straight from the route — no boundary mapping... 'return row;' ... ships whatever shape findRowById returns... directly to the HTTP client."

expectations.text: G4: Proposes concrete restructuring: a use case that the route calls, with domain rule enforcement and mapping at the boundary
expectations.evidence: Adds GetInvoiceUseCase/PayInvoiceUseCase; PayInvoiceUseCase calls invoice.markPaid() before save(); route reduced to validate/call-use-case/map via toInvoiceResponse.
